report.summary: The change does what it says: protectedFileHashes treats a SandboxFileError with code ENOENT from Files.readFile as an absent file (null hash, the same as a 404), and any other readFile error still fails with RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION. That matches the spec (08/02: a run fails only when protected login files change) and the existing 404 handling, so no spec change is needed. A worker test covers a run that completes when the Codex auth.json is missing. The issues.test.tsx change waits with a cheap text query for page 2 before the role query and leaves the assertions unchanged. Nothing blocking. Two minor notes: no test covers the non-ENOENT error path, and the test fakes the SDK error with a plain Error object, so it depends on how SandboxFileError.is detects the error. I could not check that because packages are not installed in this worktree.

findings.text: No test covers the new catch branch for a non-ENOENT readFile error (for example EACCES or a container RPC failure), which should still fail the run with RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION. The project rules ask to keep failure and security coverage. Consider a runs.cases.ts case where readFile throws a different SandboxFileError code or a generic Error and the run ends failed with RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION.

The test throws a plain Error with name/code assigned, not a real SandboxFileError. That only exercises the production branch if SandboxFileError.is() checks the shape of the error rather than using instanceof. I could not check the SDK because packages are not installed here. Throwing a real SandboxFileError instance from @cloudflare/sandbox would tie the test to the SDK's real error type.
